etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French hydrogène, coined by Louis-Bernard Guyton de Morveau and Antoine Lavoisier, from Ancient Greek ὕδωρ (húdōr, “water”) + γεννάω (gennáō, “I bring forth”). Corresponding to hydro- +‎ -gen.

definitions.definition: The lightest chemical element (symbol H), with an atomic number of 1 and atomic weight of 1.00794.
A molecule of this molecular species
Molecular hydrogen (H2), a colourless, odourless and flammable gas at room temperature.
The isotope hydrogen-1 (also symbol H), contrasting with deuterium and tritium
